Review personal use terms
Welcome to BarKey
A barcode and QR scanner keyboard that scans locally and inserts results into the text field you choose.
Enable BarKey
Android requires you to enable each keyboard yourself. Review Android’s keyboard warning, then enable BarKey in the system settings.
Open keyboard settings
Select BarKey
Use Android’s keyboard picker to choose BarKey whenever you want to scan. You can switch back to your usual keyboard at any time.
Open keyboard picker
Allow camera access
Camera access is used only for live scanning. You can grant permission in Android’s permission prompt or revoke it later in settings.
Start scanning

Open any app and tap its text field. Choose BarKey with the keyboard picker, then point the rear camera at a barcode or QR code. BarKey inserts the decoded value at the cursor.\n\nUse Switch Keyboard to return to another keyboard, or Hide Keyboard to dismiss BarKey.
Choose keyboard

Scanning controls
Fast — The default mode for ordinary barcodes.
Accurate — Adds processing for difficult, angled or damaged barcodes, but may be slower.

Preview — Shows detected values as selectable suggestions instead of inserting them automatically. Tap a suggestion to insert its complete value. Suggestions are temporary, expire automatically and are not saved as scan history.

Focus — Starts with a large scan area. Drag it over the barcode and use the see-through corner arrow to resize it. Keep the full code and a little clear space around it inside the area; enlarge it if a scan is missed. Long-press Focus to reset the area. This selects where BarKey scans; tapping the camera image requests autofocus.

Single Scan — Allows one successful scan per recognised text field. Move to another recognised field to scan again. Undoing a scan makes an otherwise empty field available again. Some apps do not reliably identify field changes.
Torch — Turns on the camera light when the device supports it.
Tap to focus — Tap the live camera image to request autofocus at that location.
Editing and navigation
Undo — Repeatedly undo up to 20 recent BarKey scans or Space insertions, one at a time, while BarKey can safely verify the editor context.
Backspace — Deletes selected text or the previous character. Hold to repeat deletion.
Left / Right arrows — Move the cursor within the text field.
Space — Inserts a space.
Tab — Requests navigation to the next field only when the app supports the appropriate action; it does not guarantee focus movement.
Enter — Performs the field’s Enter action, which may submit, advance or insert a newline depending on the app.
Keyboard controls
Switch Keyboard — Switches to another installed Android keyboard, or opens Android’s keyboard picker when needed.
Hide Keyboard — Dismisses BarKey.
Resize handle — Drag the handle above the camera preview to change BarKey’s height.

For nearby codes, use Focus to move or resize the region around the right barcode. Keep the full code and some clear space inside the region; enlarge it if a scan is missed. Use Preview to choose a detected value before insertion, or Single Scan to allow one successful scan in each field. Focus works with either option; Preview and Single Scan cannot be on together.
More detailed information is available through the ? button on the BarKey scanner.

About and Help
Close
Close About and Help and return to scanning
BarKey — Developed by Amanda Hernow. A free, offline barcode and QR scanner keyboard for Android.
Scan barcodes and QR codes directly into text fields instead of typing them by hand.
Our Privacy Commitment
Free for personal use
No subscriptions, purchases or paid features.
No Advertisements
No advertising or advertising SDKs.
No Tracking
No analytics, telemetry or user tracking.
No Accounts

No registration or login is required. The accepted personal-use terms revision is stored on this device only. If setup was skipped, BarKey opens the agreement the first time the keyboard is selected. It asks again only when the agreement text or licence changes.
Works Offline
Barcode recognition takes place entirely on this device.
No Data Collection
BarKey does not upload or persist scanned barcode contents.

Decoded text is held temporarily in memory while it is processed. Preview keeps distinct values currently visible to the decoder so you can choose one; each suggestion expires shortly after it is no longer detected. Duplicate suppression keeps the most recent accepted value in the active input session and compares it during a one-second window. Safe Undo may temporarily retain up to 20 recent BarKey insertions and bounded nearby text for each; its history is cleared when the field or cursor context changes, a non-scan editing action is used, the keyboard is hidden or switched, the input session ends, or BarKey restarts. Undo history is never saved to storage. Scan contents are not written to logs or persistent storage.
How to Use BarKey
1. Enable BarKey in Android keyboard settings.
2. Select BarKey as the active keyboard.
3. Tap the field where the scanned value should appear.
4. Point the rear camera at a barcode or QR code.
5. BarKey inserts the scanned value at the cursor in that field.
6. Use the editing and navigation controls to continue working.
Fast — The default mode. Prioritises quick scanning of normal, clearly printed barcodes.
Accurate — Uses additional processing for difficult, angled, damaged or inverted barcodes. It may be slower.
Tap to focus — Tap the camera preview to request focus at that location.
Torch — On supported devices, tap the flashlight icon to illuminate the scanning area.

Preview — Turn this on to see distinct detected values and choose which one to insert, especially when several codes are close together. Tap the required suggestion. Automatic insertion pauses while Preview is on; suggestions disappear when codes are no longer detected. Preview cannot be used with Single Scan. The Java fallback may find fewer codes than ZXing-C++.

Focus — Turn this on to scan inside the outlined region. It starts large so a code is easier to capture; drag it over the barcode and use the small see-through corner arrow to resize it. Keep the full code and a little clear space around it inside the region; enlarge it if scans are missed. Long-press Focus to reset the region. BarKey decodes only inside this area using the selected Fast or Accurate mode. This is separate from tapping the camera preview to request autofocus and exposure.

Single Scan — Turn this on to accept one successfully inserted barcode in each text field. It is useful on serial-number or inventory forms where each field should receive one code. Move to another field to scan again; Enter or Tab does not by itself prove that focus changed. Undoing a scan makes an otherwise empty field available again. Focus works with Single Scan, but Preview cannot be used with it. Some apps do not tell Android clearly when a field changes, so BarKey may not always be able to recognise the new field. Turn Single Scan off to return to continuous scanning.

Combining features — Focus works with Preview or Single Scan. Use Focus to move or resize the scan area. Preview lets you choose a detected value before insertion; Single Scan allows one successful scan in each field. Preview and Single Scan cannot be used together. Fast and Accurate remain independent choices.

Undo — Repeatedly undo up to 20 recent BarKey scans or Space insertions, one at a time, while bounded editor context still matches. A configured Enter or Tab suffix may submit or move focus; Undo cannot reverse that action. Undo is disabled for password/private fields and unsafe selections.
Left / Right — Move the cursor within the current field.
Backspace — Tap to delete the selection or previous character. Press and hold to repeat deletion.
Space — Insert a space at the cursor.

Tab — Requests the Next action only when the editor explicitly advertises forward navigation. Otherwise BarKey does nothing: it does not inject a Tab key, submit the form or hide the keyboard. Chrome, WebView and other apps control focus traversal.
Enter — Perform the field action, or insert a newline in a multiline field when appropriate. Enter actions and inserted newlines cannot be undone.
Switch Keyboard — Return to the previous keyboard when Android supports it, or open the system keyboard picker.

Tab and Enter behaviour depends on the receiving application and the field. BarKey cannot control arbitrary focus traversal inside another app. Tab is intentionally a no-op unless the field advertises NEXT navigation; an app may still handle an advertised action in its own way.
Resize BarKey by dragging the small handle above the camera preview. The keyboard stays docked; its preview grows or shrinks while editing controls keep their normal size.
Permissions

BarKey requests Camera permission so it can scan barcodes and QR codes. Camera access is needed for scanning. You can deny permission or revoke it later in Android Settings; scanning will be unavailable until it is granted again.

Android may show its standard warning when you enable a third-party keyboard because an input method can receive text entered into fields. BarKey uses the active field to insert scans and performs editing actions when you request them.

BarKey’s app manifest removes Internet and network-state permissions, and source review found no app networking calls. Scanning needs no internet, account or login. BarKey does not request access to files, contacts, location or the microphone.

About BarKey

BarKey is an Android input method, free for private personal use, that uses the rear camera to scan supported barcodes and QR codes. Recognition happens on this device. Scanned text is inserted into the active text field through Android’s input-method interface.

I create free software to make useful tools accessible without unnecessary subscriptions, advertisements, tracking or paywalls. Optional donations support my development; they do not unlock features or benefits.
